previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with T1-T2 paraplegia and chronic obstructive lung disease, was admitted after being found hypoxic during a clinic visit, with oxygen saturation of 80%. She had a productive cough with yellow sputum and was subsequently diagnosed with sepsis secondary to a urinary tract infection caused by Klebsiella pneumoniae, which was treated with meropenem and transitioned to ertapenem for outpatient therapy. She also had hypoxemia and evidence of left lower lobe atelectasis with possible superimposed infection, managed with vancomycin and ciprofloxacin. She required ICU-level care initially for septic shock, supported with fluids and vasopressors, and was stabilized within 24 hours. A PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic administration. Her chronic respiratory failure and hypercapnia were managed with oxygen and bronchodilators. She improved clinically, was weaned to 2.5 liters of oxygen, and was discharged home with home health services for IV antibiotics and follow-up care.

INDICATION:  ___ female with hypertension, questionable aspiration
event at nursing home.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph from ___ and CTA chest from ___.

CHEST, AP AND LATERAL:  Patient was unable to raise her arms for the lateral
view, on which bilateral humeral fixation plates and screws obscure
evaluation.

Left internal jugular catheter has been removed.  Right PICC again terminates
in the mid SVC.  There is no pneumothorax.  

The lungs are overinflated.  Moderate cardiomegaly persists, with vascular
congestion and small bilateral pleural effusions.  Lower lobe opacities
persist, left greater than right. 
 
There are old healed bilateral rib fractures, with associated chest wall
deformity.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Chronic obstructive airways disease.  
2.  Congestive heart failure.
3.  Bilateral lower lobe opacities may be secondary to #2, but superimposed
pneumonia is not excluded.

HISTORY:  Hypoxia with shortness of breath and fever, to assess for
aspiration.

FINDINGS:  In comparison with the study of ___, allowing for changes in
patient obliquity, there is probably little overall change.  Continued
enlargement of the cardiac silhouette with elevation of pulmonary venous
pressure.  Bibasilar opacifications, more prominent in the retrocardiac
region, most likely represents atelectasis and effusion.  The possibility of
superimposed pneumonia cannot be definitely excluded.

The right paravertebral mass seen on CT is difficult to appreciate.

AP CHEST, 4:33 A.M., ___

HISTORY:  Paraplegia.  Hypoxia, fever, and dyspnea.

IMPRESSION:  AP chest compared to ___ and ___:

Severe cardiomegaly is chronic, worse now than it was in ___.  The same can
be said for bibasilar atelectasis and moderate right pleural effusion and
mediastinal vascular engorgement although it has not been much changed since
___.  Findings suggest chronic heart failure, particularly right-sided. 
Pericardial effusion and pneumonia are not excluded.

HISTORY:  A ___ woman with pneumonia and UTI with poor access, failed
attempts before.

OPERATORS:  Dr. ___, Dr. ___, and Dr. ___
(attending physician), performed the procedure.

ANESTHESIA:  Local anesthesia was provided by 1% lidocaine.

PROCEDURE:  Verbal informed consent was obtained from the patient after
explaining the procedure, risks, benefits, and alternatives.  She was brought
to the angio table and laid supine on the table.  Both the right and left arms
were prepped and draped in a sterile fashion.  A preprocedural huddle and
timeout were performed per ___ protocol.

Initially, a PICC was attempted to be placed on the right arm, but after
multiple attempts of getting blood back, the nitinol wire would not thread
into the vein.  After trying to access the brachial, cephalic and basilic
veins in the right arm, it was decided to try to access a vein on the left
arm.  Multiple attempts were made to access the brachial, cephalic and basilic
veins on the left arm, but a similar train of events in which there would be
ultrasound evidence of vein entry and blood return, but both the nitinol and
headhunter wire would not thread into the vein.  Since the patient was having
some considerable discomfort from lying on the table for about an hour and a
half and since the wire refuse to thread in, the procedure was abandoned.  The
on call person Dr. ___ was informed about this and was given the option of
either a temporary central line or tunneled power central line through the
internal jugular veins.  This was conveyed at 7:15 p.m. on ___.

The patient towards the end of the procedure was having considerable
discomfort in her back from lying on the table.  There were no immediate
complications.

IMPRESSION:  Unsuccessful placement of PICC line in both the right and left
arms.

INDICATION:  T1-T2 paraplegia, status post MVC, recurrent pneumonias, assess
cause of dysphagia.

TECHNIQUE:  Oropharyngeal swallowing videofluoroscopy was performed in
conjunction with speech and swallow division.  Multiple consistencies of
barium were administered.

FINDINGS:  There was penetration and aspiration of nectar-thick barium and
aspiration of thin liquids.  The chin tuck helps prevent aspiration with thin
liquids; however, penetration is still present.

IMPRESSION:  Penetration and aspiration with thin liquids.  Chin tuck helps to
limit aspiration with thin liquids.  Penetration with nectar-thick liquids. 
For details, please refer to speech and swallow division note in OMR.

HISTORY:  ___ woman with recurrent UTIs and pneumonia, needing IV
antibiotics.  The patient was not able to receive a PICC line, so she is
getting a tunneled power double-lumen line.

OPERATORS:  Dr. ___ and Dr. ___ performed the
procedure.

ANESTHESIA:  The procedure was performed with local lidocaine and a single
dose of 0.5 mg of SQ Dilaudid (as the patient had no IV access).  

PROCEDURE:  Written informed consent was obtained from the patient after
explaining the procedure, risks, benefits, and alternatives to it.  The
patient was brought to the angio table and laid supine on the table.  The
right side of the neck and chest were prepped and draped in a sterile fashion.
A pre-procedural huddle and timeout were performed per ___ protocol.

Right patent IJ was accessed with a micropuncture needle under ultrasound
guidance.  Then, a 0.018 guidewire was introduced through the needle and
confirmed to be in the right atrium fluoroscopically.  After the skin ___,
the needle was exchanged for a micropuncture sheath.

Then, attention was now directed to the right chest where a suitable tunneling
point was chosen four fingerbreadths below the venotomy site.  This was
anesthetized by utilizing 1% lidocaine.  The prospective tunnel was
anesthetized using lidocaine with epinephrine.  Then, the tunneling was
performed with the tunneler that was provided.  The venotomy site was then
dilated using a 6 ___ dilator.  Then, the peel-away sheath was placed in
the venotomy site and once the inner dilator and wire were removed, catheter
was thread in and finally a fluoroscopic image demonstrated the presence of
the catheter tip in the right atrium.  The venotomy site was closed with ___
Vicryl and the catheter was sutured with 0 silk.  Both lumens withdrew and
flush easily.  Sterile dressing was applied.

The patient tolerated the procedure well and had no immediate complications.

IMPRESSION:  Successful placement of a dual-lumen power tunneled line in the
right IJ.  The tip is in the right atrium.  The line is ready to use.

microbiology.comments: No respiratory viruses isolated.  Culture screened for Adenovirus, Influenza A & B, Parainfluenza type 1,2 & 3, and Respiratory Syncytial Virus.  Detection of viruses other than those listed above will only be performed on specific request. Please call Virology at ___ within 1 week if additional testing is needed.

Negative for Respiratory Viral Antigen.  Specimen screened for: Adeno, Parainfluenza 1, 2, 3, Influenza A, B, and RSV by immunofluorescence.  Refer to respiratory viral culture for further information.

NEGATIVE FOR LEGIONELLA SEROGROUP 1 ANTIGEN.            (Reference Range-Negative).  Performed by Immunochromogenic assay.  A negative result does not rule out infection due to other L. pneumophila serogroups or other Legionella species. Furthermore, in infected patients the excretion of antigen in urine may vary.
